note: byte equality with the source proves faithful transfer, not substantive completeness

residual_risks.RR1: `/media/*` is closed (403) in Phase 1, so OB29's "static /media with Range support" is delivered as configuration that is tested for Range support only in a throwaway Caddy container and is not reachable in the running stack until jade-u8z adds the signed-URL check of ADR 0007; seeking on real devices is first proven in Phase 4.
residual_risks.RR10: OB30's "22 from deploy source only" cannot be met as written with hosted CI runners, whose addresses change; the deploy path (a self-hosted runner, the provider's firewall API, a VPN, or a pull-based deploy) has to be chosen with jade-0za, and until then jade-4zw's firewall rule is undefined.
residual_risks.RR11: The image base is Alpine (musl) to stay well under 300 MB; a later native dependency without musl builds, for example an argon2 binding in Phase 3, would force a move to a Debian slim base and a new size check.
residual_risks.RR12: Phase 1 changes Mike's machine (a user-level pnpm install that edits `~/.bashrc`, and OS libraries for WebKit installed with sudo); without them jade-h8i cannot meet OB1, and a Windows-side pnpm shim on the WSL `PATH` can shadow the right pnpm when `PATH` is not set explicitly.
residual_risks.RR13: A free host port is found by binding port 0 and closing the socket, so another process can take it before the test or Compose binds it; that shows as a start-up failure, retried up to three times with a new port, never as a check passing against another process, but on a busy machine it can still fail a gate and count toward the three-failures stop.
residual_risks.RR14: On staging the previous app container is replaced when the deploy switches to a candidate that passed its readiness check, so if the check through Caddy after the switch then fails, the previous version is not running until the script's rollback is ready again (bounded by its timeouts, measured in the rehearsal); keeping the previous container through that check needs two app services and an upstream switch in Caddy, left to jade-kn0 for production.
residual_risks.RR2: With no git remote and no CI host, the workflow of jade-xu0 has never run; OB10, OB11, OB12, OB36, OB46 and OB49 cannot be verified, the 10-minute budget rests on estimates and on local timings from a 32-CPU machine, and the first run on the real host may need fixes.
residual_risks.RR3: jade-4zw and the staging exit criterion stay blocked by the human bead jade-0za, so ADR 0014's "Staging exists before feature work" is not met if Phase 2 starts first, and deploy problems would then surface later than the phase goal intends.
residual_risks.RR4: The tool majors are newer than anything the planner could run (SvelteKit 3.2, Vite 8, pnpm 12, Vitest 5, ESLint 10, TypeScript 6, Caddy 2.11): the design was checked against registries and published documentation only and nothing was installed, so file names, option names or CLI flags may differ at implementation; the black-box checks hold regardless, but a difference that changes a mechanism has to come back to planloop.
residual_risks.RR5: Request log lines are written for every request, including requests from kits with logging off; they carry no kit, class, session or step identifier, and this plan reads that as outside CLAUDE.md rule 2 on the strength of PRIVACY.md's server-logs row, a reading in the same family as the open threat-model item TM-5.
residual_risks.RR6: Error messages are never written to the JSON logs (only the error's type, tag and stack frames), which protects rule 4 but makes failures on staging and production harder to diagnose.
residual_risks.RR7: Two outputs fall outside the JSON log contract: adapter-node's start-up line, which is plain text and shows the server's own bind address, and requests for static assets, which the adapter serves before `handle` and which therefore get no log line and no request id.
residual_risks.RR8: Compatibility of a migration with the previous app version cannot be proven in general; the destructive-statement guard and the old-app-on-new-schema job catch structural breaks, not semantic ones such as a column whose meaning changed or a backfill the old code misreads.
residual_risks.RR9: In the Compose stacks the owner role `jade_owner` is the superuser of the official Postgres image, so migrations run with superuser rights; the app never holds those credentials, and a managed database (ARCHITECTURE.md extension point E7) would need the role bootstrap revisited.
